title: LRU Cache with Doubly Linked List & Hash Map
description: Guarantees strict constant time amortized operations for get() and put() by pinning sentinel nodes to head and tail.
notes: Key takeaway: Sentinel head and tail nodes eliminate null pointer checks during node detachment. When evicting, pop from head.next; when accessing or adding, push directly before tail. The hash map stores direct node references for O(1) pointer updates.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Sentinel head & tail nodes prevent null checks on edge insertions.

title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path with Min-Priority Queue
description: Adjacency-list formulation using std::greater comparator over a min-heap for single-source shortest path.
notes: Important concept: std::priority_queue defaults to max-heap in C++; std::greater<T> inverts it to a min-heap. The lazy deletion check `if (d > dist[u]) continue;` is crucial because vertices are re-pushed upon discovering shorter paths. Never run Dijkstra on graphs with negative edge weights!

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Invariant check: dist[u] < d prevents redundant relaxations on lazy deletions in binary heap!

title: Debounce & Throttle Hook Implementation
description: Type-safe React hooks handling cleanup timers, leading/trailing execution flags for fast search & resize handlers.
notes: Debounce buffers high-frequency user actions until a pause occurs (e.g. live search typing). Throttle guarantees execution at fixed maximum intervals (e.g. scroll handlers). In React, always clean up timers inside useEffect to prevent memory leaks and setState on unmounted components.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Cleanup function in useEffect cancels pending timer on rapid prop changes.

title: Fast I/O & Modular Arithmetic Template
description: Competitive programming I/O acceleration template with binary exponentiation and Fermat's Little Theorem modular inverse.
notes: ios_base::sync_with_stdio(false) disables synchronization between C++ streams and C stdio. cin.tie(NULL) unties cin from cout. Fermat's Little Theorem states a^(p-1) = 1 (mod p), meaning modular inverse a^(-1) = a^(p-2) (mod p) for prime p.

title: Container With Most Water (Greedy Two-Pointer)
description: Optimal two-pointer contraction maximizing area between vertical lines by always advancing the shorter line.
notes: Mathematical proof: The area is constrained by min(height[left], height[right]) * width. Moving the taller pointer can only decrease width without any chance of increasing the bottleneck height. Therefore, discarding the shorter pointer is guaranteed never to eliminate the optimal pair.
code:
def maxArea(height: list[int]) -> int:
    left, right = 0, len(height) - 1
    max_water = 0
    
    while left < right:
        width = right - left
        current_height = min(height[left], height[right])
        max_water = max(max_water, width * current_height)
        
        # Invariant: Moving the taller pointer can never yield a larger area
        # because width shrinks and bottleneck is constrained by min height.
        if height[left] < height[right]:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
            
    return max_water

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Mathematical invariant: The eliminated line cannot pair with any remaining candidate to exceed current area.

title: Thread-Safe Ring Buffer (Producer-Consumer)
description: Lock-free bounded circular queue synchronization primitives using atomic head/tail cursors.
notes: Ordering::Acquire on load ensures we read all prior writes made by the producer. Ordering::Release on store ensures that our buffer slot write is visible to other threads before the updated index is published. This guarantees lock-free safety.

title: Recursive CTE Hierarchical Graph & Tree Traversal
description: PostgreSQL recursive common table expression detecting cyclical dependencies and computing topological depth.
notes: Recursive CTEs consist of an Anchor member (base rows) and a Recursive member (joined iteratively). To prevent infinite loops in cyclic graphs, track visited path IDs via ARRAY[id] and filter with `WHERE NOT (c.id = ANY(ct.path))`.
code:
WITH RECURSIVE category_tree AS (
    -- Base member: root nodes
    SELECT 
        id, 
        name, 
        parent_id, 
        1 AS depth, 
        ARRAY[id] AS path
    FROM course_categories
    WHERE parent_id IS NULL

    UNION ALL

    -- Recursive member: join children with cycle prevention
    SELECT 
        c.id, 
        c.name, 
        c.parent_id, 
        ct.depth + 1, 
        path || c.id
    FROM course_categories c
    INNER JOIN category_tree ct ON c.parent_id = ct.id
    WHERE NOT (c.id = ANY(ct.path))
)
SELECT id, name, depth, path 
FROM category_tree 
ORDER BY path;

testCases.input: Categories 5 levels deep with cyclic reference at node 4
testCases.expected: Terminates gracefully at depth 5 without infinite loop

title: Left-Leaning Red-Black Tree Balance Invariants
description: Sedgewick 2-3 Left-Leaning Red-Black (LLRB) tree rotation and color flip algorithms preserving 1-to-1 isometry.
notes: Left-Leaning Red-Black trees simplify classical Red-Black trees by enforcing that red links only lean left. Right-leaning red links are immediately fixed by rotateLeft(); consecutive red links are fixed by rotateRight() followed by flipColors().

title: Merge Sort with Divide-and-Conquer Invariants
description: Stable O(N log N) divide-and-conquer sorting algorithm with recursive subproblem decomposition and two-pointer merge.
notes: Key invariant: The merge step assumes both sub-arrays are already sorted in non-decreasing order. Space complexity is O(N) for auxiliary buffer arrays during merging. Guaranteed O(N log N) worst-case time makes it ideal when predictable performance is required.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Stability check: using <= rather than < preserves relative order of equal keys!

title: Trie Prefix Tree with Autocomplete & Search
description: High-performance n-ary tree structure for fast string dictionary storage, prefix filtering, and vocabulary lookup.
notes: Key takeaway: Each node stores child pointers keyed by character and a boolean flag isEndOfWord. Search and insertion operate in O(L) where L is the string length, strictly independent of the total number of words in the dictionary.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: O(L) lookup independent of vocabulary size N — essential for search suggestion engines.

title: Kadane's Dynamic Programming Algorithm (Maximum Subarray)
description: Computes the contiguous subarray within a one-dimensional numerical array that has the largest sum in optimal O(N) time and O(1) space.
notes: Mathematical proof: At index i, the maximum subarray ending at i is max(nums[i], maxEndingHere + nums[i]). If running sum drops below 0, discarding previous elements and starting fresh from nums[i] is always provably optimal.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Boundary invariant: Tracking tempStart allows exact [start, end] window coordinates recovery.

title: Kahn's Topological Sort with BFS Cycle Detection
description: Linear ordering of vertices in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) using vertex in-degrees and BFS queue, detecting cycles if output length < V.
notes: Algorithmic guarantee: Only nodes with in-degree == 0 can be processed at any step. If all vertices are processed, the graph is provably a DAG. If visited count < V, a directed cyclic dependency exists (crucial for build systems like Make and course prerequisites).

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Cycle invariant: if topoOrder.size() < n, at least one directed cycle was skipped.

title: Thread-Safe Shared State with Arc<RwLock<T>>
description: Idiomatic Rust concurrency pattern enabling concurrent multiple readers or exclusive single writer under compiler-enforced borrow checks.
notes: Key takeaway: `Arc<RwLock<T>>` guarantees safe data sharing across threads without data races. Multiple readers acquire shared locks concurrently; writers acquire exclusive mutable locks, preventing stale reads and torn writes with zero garbage collection.

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Send + Sync invariants: Arc provides atomic reference counting while RwLock prevents data races.

title: Rolling 7-Day Window Moving Average & Partition LAG
description: Advanced analytic SQL using OVER(), PARTITION BY, sliding window ROWS BETWEEN frames, and LAG() delta calculations.
notes: Key takeaway: Window functions compute cumulative or moving aggregates without collapsing rows like GROUP BY. `ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` ensures exact physical frame bounds for moving average and trend detection.
code:
WITH DailyUserMetrics AS (
    SELECT
        student_id,
        event_date,
        snippets_created,
        LAG(snippets_created, 1) OVER (
            PARTITION BY student_id
            ORDER BY event_date
        ) AS prev_day_snippets
    FROM student_study_log
)
SELECT
    student_id,
    event_date,
    snippets_created,
    (snippets_created - COALESCE(prev_day_snippets, 0)) AS day_over_day_delta,
    ROUND(AVG(snippets_created) OVER (
        PARTITION BY student_id
        ORDER BY event_date
        ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ), 2) AS rolling_7day_avg,
    SUM(snippets_created) OVER (
        PARTITION BY student_id
        ORDER BY event_date
    ) AS cumulative_study_snippets
FROM DailyUserMetrics
ORDER BY student_id, event_date;

annotations.author: Bhoomika Yadav
annotations.note: Analytical frame invariant: ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING calculates exact 7-day rolling window.
